approachQuestion.prompt: Evaluate an expression with NUM(v), DIV(a,b), and IFZERO(test,whenZero,otherwise). DIV evaluates a then b and returns integer division truncated toward zero, or ERROR if b is zero or an evaluated child is ERROR. IFZERO evaluates test first, then evaluates only whenZero if test is zero, or only otherwise if it is nonzero. An evaluated ERROR propagates. Examples: IFZERO(NUM(0),NUM(7),DIV(NUM(1),NUM(0))) returns 7; DIV(NUM(-7),NUM(2)) returns -3.
constraints: The input is a read-only unshared expression tree with n nodes, 1 ≤ n ≤ 100000, height h ≤ 1000.
All evaluated non-error operations fit signed 64-bit integers. Arithmetic, tag access, and tagged error handling take constant time.
Dead branches can contain division by zero; they must not be evaluated.

options.text: Recursively return a tagged value or ERROR. For IFZERO, first obtain test, then recurse into exactly the selected branch; for DIV follow its stated child order and error rules.
options.feedback: Demanded branches follow the definition, and failures in unselected branches remain unobserved.

options.text: Use an explicit stack of evaluator frames with node, stage, and saved child result. IFZERO frames schedule only the selected branch after test completes.
options.feedback: This models the same pending work and preserves branch selection, child order, and errors without language recursion.

options.text: Evaluate every child of every node first, propagating any error, then choose which IFZERO value to return.
options.feedback: The first example must return 7 even though its dead branch divides by zero.

options.text: For IFZERO choose whenZero whenever test is nonzero and otherwise when test is zero.

feedback.reason: IFZERO evaluates only its selected branch.
details: The recursive evaluator returns a tagged number or ERROR. Evaluate DIV children left to right and reject a zero divisor. At IFZERO, evaluate test and propagate its ERROR; otherwise evaluate just the branch selected by the numeric test and forward that result. There is no prewalk of unselected branches.

IFZERO evaluates only its selected branch. An error in an unselected branch must not fail the expression. DIV still evaluates its demanded operands in order and rejects zero divisor; tagged errors are not ordinary numbers.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze method-1 as described in the revealed method. Let n and h have the meanings in Q1. Use child indices and references without copying lists. Count active call frames; exclude input and returned output. There is no tail-call elimination. No hashing is used. Here n is expression node count and h is expression height. Analyze the recursive method-1, not the explicit-stack alternative. Choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair among the options.

feedback.reason: Each demanded node is evaluated once; only its active ancestor path remains live.
details: Each demanded node is evaluated at most once; a legal input can demand all n nodes, for example a nested chain of DIV nodes. Active calls follow one path and hold constant-sized tags and results.
“O(n) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: Nested calls remain active along a path; their storage must be counted.
“O(n²) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: Each object is processed once without rescanning or copying its descendants.
“O(h + 1) time, O(h + 1) auxiliary space”: A shallow but wide input can still require inspecting every object.
